sections.h2: Does Virginia have an estate or inheritance tax?
sections.html:
No. Virginia no longer charges an estate tax or an inheritance tax, so an heir does not owe the state a death tax just for receiving a house.

Older advice still circulates because the rules changed. Before July 1, 2007, Virginia had an estate tax equal to the federal credit for state death taxes. When the federal credit was eliminated, the Virginia tax was effectively repealed with it.

One narrow exception remains: certain remainder interests are still subject to the inheritance tax. Public Document 15-93 has a section on Virginia estate and inheritance taxes that covers them. If the house passes through a life estate or a trust with a remainder, ask a probate attorney or the Department of Taxation before you assume the answer is zero.

sections.h2: Taxes and fees at a glance
sections.html:
ChargeAmountWho it affects
Estate taxNone today; repealed in effect after July 1, 2007Heirs of any house
Inheritance taxNone, except certain remainder interestsHeirs of life estates or trust remainders
Probate tax10 cents per $100 of estate valueEstates over $15,000
Deed grantor tax50 cents per $500 of considerationWhoever signs the sale deed

The probate tax and the deed tax are covered below.

The probate tax is a different charge from an estate tax. It is imposed when a will is probated or an administrator is appointed, and it is based on the value of the estate rather than on who inherits.

Under Code 58.1-1712 the rate is 10 cents for every $100 of value, or fraction of $100. It does not apply to decedents' estates of $15,000 or less. Value is determined under the next section, 58.1-1713.

For current steps and any filing fees, ask the circuit court clerk in the city or county where the person lived.

sections.h2: Who can sell an inherited house?
sections.html:
When the will tells the executor to sell the real estate, the executor has the power to sell and convey it and to receive the proceeds, provided no one else was named to sell. Code 64.2-521 says so directly.

If no executor qualifies, or those who qualified die, resign, or are removed, an administrator with the will annexed holds that same power unless the will clearly says otherwise.

Before you list, gather these:

  • The will and the certificate showing who is the personal representative.
  • Any direction in the will to sell the real estate.
  • The deed, the latest tax bill, and any mortgage statement.
  • A list of what the title company needs from the clerk's office before closing.

No Virginia estate tax payment is part of that list. Ask the title company which authority papers it wants to see.

sections.h2: Property tax still attached to the house
sections.html:
Real estate tax stays with the house after a death, and it has a priority that surprises many heirs. Code 58.1-3340 puts the lien for real estate tax ahead of every other lien or encumbrance, and it stays until the taxing authority is actually paid.

Penalties and interest count as taxes under that section, and proceeds at a sale must go to taxes and levies on the real estate first. The seller's share is prorated by contract, so the purchase agreement should say who covers which dates.

Local rules vary by city and county. In Virginia Beach, for example, installments are due December 5 and June 5, late payments carry a 10% penalty or $10, whichever is greater, plus interest at 9.6% a year, and a lien can be recorded with the Circuit Court clerk if taxes stay unpaid. Once taxes are three years plus the current tax year delinquent, the Treasurer may advertise the property and charges a $25 fee.

If you inherit a house with taxes behind, ask the local Treasurer for a payoff figure before listing. The title company pays it from the sale proceeds.

The sale deed carries the same grantor tax as any other Virginia sale. Code 58.1-802 sets it at 50 cents for each $500 of consideration or fraction of it, paid by the grantor unless the parties agree the grantee will pay some or all.

The clerk will not record a deed unless the consideration is stated on its first page and the clerk has certified that the tax was paid. The tax is collected through the clerk and shared between the state and the locality.

Whether the estate or the buyer bears it follows the contract.

sections.h2: Federal tax on an inherited sale
sections.html:
Federal income tax can still apply to gain, even though Virginia has no estate tax. If you received the house by inheritance, your basis is figured under special rules in IRS Publication 551, Basis of Assets, not by the usual cost rule. Property acquired from a decedent also has its own holding-period exceptions, covered in Publication 544. Whether a gain exists at all depends on the basis and the sale price.

  • Ask the estate's tax preparer how basis was set for the house.
  • The $250,000 and $500,000 home sale exclusion requires that you owned and used the home as your main residence for 24 months out of the last 5 years.
  • If you receive Form 1099-S, report the sale even when the gain is excludable.
  • A loss on a personal-use home is not deductible.

A separate page on this site explains how the federal rules interact with Virginia income tax on a house sale.

sections.h2: When an as-is cash sale helps an estate
sections.html:
It helps when the family wants a closing date instead of repairs, and when carrying costs are rising. Real estate tax, insurance, utilities, and yard care continue for as long as the estate holds the house, and a vacant house adds its own risks.

An as-is sale skips repair negotiations, which matters when heirs live in different states. Title and closing still go through a title company, and the personal representative must have authority to convey.

We can walk through the paperwork with you and answer questions about timing. We are not tax or legal advisors, and a probate attorney should confirm who may sign.

faqs.q: Does Virginia charge an inheritance tax on a house I inherit?
faqs.a: No. Virginia has no inheritance tax, with a narrow exception for certain remainder interests. Ask a probate attorney if the house came through a life estate or trust remainder.

faqs.q: What is the Virginia probate tax rate?
faqs.a: The probate tax is 10 cents for every $100 of estate value under Code 58.1-1712, and it does not apply to estates of $15,000 or less.

faqs.q: Can an executor sell the house without all heirs signing?
faqs.a: If the will directs the real estate to be sold and names no one else to sell it, the executor has the power to sell and convey under Code 64.2-521. Other situations depend on the will, so confirm with an attorney.

faqs.q: Who pays the real estate tax owed on an inherited house at closing?
faqs.a: It is paid from the sale proceeds. The tax lien has priority over other liens under Code 58.1-3340, and the contract prorates the seller's share.

faqs.q: Do I owe federal tax when I sell an inherited house?
faqs.a: Possibly. Federal income tax applies to gain, and inherited property has its own basis rules in Publication 551. Many sales produce little or no gain, but confirm with a tax professional.
